references.text: Repeats the command to rest on the seventh day, including slaves and foreigners, so that they may rest.
Emphasizes the Sabbath as a day of rest for the Lord, where no work is to be done.
Reiterates the prohibition against working on the Sabbath, the seventh day.
Parallel passage in Deuteronomy repeating the Sabbath command with the same inclusion of son, daughter, male slave, female slave, livestock, and foreigner.
Describes the Sabbath as a holy assembly where no work is to be done.
The basis for the Sabbath command: God rested on the seventh day after creation and made it holy.
Isaiah speaks of the blessing of keeping the Sabbath and honoring it by not pursuing one's own affairs.
Jeremiah warns against carrying burdens and working on the Sabbath day.
Nehemiah rebukes the people for working and conducting business on the Sabbath.
Jesus heals on the Sabbath and points out that even animals are cared for on this day.
Jesus teaches that the Sabbath was made for man, and that the Son of Man is Lord of the Sabbath.
Jesus defends his disciples who pick grain on the Sabbath and declares himself Lord of the Sabbath.
Exodus 16:29 shows the historical practice of the Sabbath before the law was given, emphasizing that rest is a gift from God.
